title: Exercise 2 – A portfolio with a short sale
text: You have EUR 5,000 to invest. You sell short Carrefour stock worth EUR 2,500 and buy Pernod Ricard stock worth EUR 7,500. The returns of the two stocks have a correlation of 0.25.

title: Exercise 3 – GameStop and the capital market line
text: A friend invests all his savings in a single stock, GameStop, with an expected return of 10% and a volatility of 50%. The market portfolio has an expected return of 8% and a volatility of 20%. The risk-free rate is 4%. Assume that the CAPM holds.

title: Exercise 4 – Campari-Milano acquires Molinari
text: Campari-Milano N.V. is all-equity financed, with an equity beta of 1.2 and a market value of EUR 2 billion. It plans to acquire its competitor Molinari S.p.A., also all-equity financed, with an equity beta of 0.6 and a market value of EUR 500 million. Campari-Milano finances the acquisition entirely with debt, which you can treat as risk-free. Assume perfect capital markets.

title: Exercise 5 – Blüthner GmbH changes its capital structure
text: Blüthner GmbH manufactures pianos. It expects a free cash flow of EUR 15 million next year, growing at 5% per year forever. Blüthner is currently all-equity financed and its cost of capital is 7%. Assume perfect capital markets (no taxes).

title: Exercise 6 – Alpha's bond
text: Three years ago, Alpha issued a 5-year bond with a face value of EUR 500 million and an annual coupon rate of 7.5%. Alpha is rated BB by Standard & Poor's. The residual maturity is now two years. The risk-free rate is 1%, and the average yield to maturity of BB-rated corporate bonds is 5%.

title: Exercise 7 – Two funds
text: Fund X has an expected return of 12% and a volatility of 25%. Fund Y has an expected return of 9% and a volatility of 15%. The risk-free rate is 3%. You can borrow and lend at the risk-free rate and want to combine exactly one of the two funds with the risk-free asset.
